title: Hyperbeat (HyperEVM) — ether.fi-lineage withdraw manager / queue accounting
closed_reasons: finalizeWithdrawals is PROTOCOL_ADMIN-only (fork test reverts NotAuthorized)
claimWithdrawal pays entry.user fixed at request time and sets claimed=true before the external call; attacker claim of another id pays that user, double claim reverts AlreadyClaimed
manager ETH balance equals the sum of the 217 finalized-unclaimed entries exactly (1621.905798325016362542 HYPE) - no surplus, no shortfall
the 2025 Critical (reverting receiver bricks finalization) is fixed by the pull pattern; fork test shows finalize still succeeds
no AtomicQueue/solver/arbitrary-call surface exists; deployed source is byte-identical to audited etherfi-protocol/beHYPE HEAD
stored exchangeRatio is only 5.68e-5 below NAV/share; instant exit costs 30 bps and queue exit locks capital 3-7 days, so the JIT yield capture is net-negative
key_facts: exchangeRatio 1.022995496666924603 vs NAV/share 1.023053582343401925 -> gap 0.0057% (720.52 USD of un-poked yield for all holders)
queue: 13 pending (632.481469192585276309 HYPE), lastFinalizedIndex 5590, 217 finalized-unclaimed = 1621.905798325016362542 HYPE == manager balance to the wei
instant: 30 bps fee, capacity 4976.17 beHYPE, low watermark 100 bps of TVL, exchangeRateGuard=true (500 bps APR)
deployed source == etherfi-protocol/beHYPE 06ee135 (2026-03-29); repo ships Certora + Nethermind NM-0628 + Bundle 9 + OFT audits
ether.fi Liquid 2026-09-11 43260 USD exploit was in legacy AtomicQueue (arbitrary external call); no AtomicQueue in beHYPE
caveats: HyperCore read precompiles are absent from the fork; delegatorSummary and spotBalance are mocked with the exact same-block values, and getTotalProtocolHype is asserted equal to the on-chain value
owner/upgrader timelock getMinDelay() is 1800s (30 min), not the 3 days the repo README claims - privileged risk over the full TVL
admin keys are 2 EOAs (PROTOCOL_ADMIN), guardian 1 EOA
JIT becomes profitable if ExchangeRatioUpdated cadence exceeds ~51 days; monitor
one_liner: external unprivileged attacker can extract ~$0 live; the queue is an exactly-funded escrow with beneficiary-bound claims, the Critical queue-DoS is fixed, and the only asymmetry (0.0057% stale ratio) is dominated by the 30 bps instant fee
